clue.text: 21 Down eclipsing mashed potato — except to mum

indicators.note: to eclipse is to block out by passing across, so one piece covers another on both sides

parts.note: 21 Down is a Scots word for turnip; neep is another Scots name for the same vegetable

indicators.note: mashed food is pulped out of its shape, so the letters lose their order
except means leaving something out, so the named letters are taken away

parts.note: taken as written, before the last two letters go

explanation.surface: A Scottish plate of neeps and tatties, with the turnip covering the mash.
explanation.walkthrough: NEEP wraps around POTA (potato without TO) rearranged. Neeps and tatties are turnip and potato, a Scottish pairing. This is one of the Across answers hiding a worm: TAPE.
explanation.definitionFit: Mum as in keeping mum means saying nothing, and not a peep is an idiom for complete silence.

clue.text: Where to find Jarrow worker's demand, 1980s-style?

parts.note: Jarrow is a town in the North East of England, abbreviated NE
pay is what a worker demands

explanation.surface: Asks where the Jarrow marchers' demands might be heard, as if recalling a protest.
explanation.walkthrough: Jarrow, a shipbuilding town in north-east England, is famous for the 1936 Jarrow March of unemployed workers. 'Where to find' puts the wage in the North East.
explanation.definitionFit: The New Age movement of alternative spirituality and music peaked during the 1980s, so the term describes that decade's fashion.

clue.text: Good egg flips worthless

indicators.note: to flip something is to turn it over, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: top means excellent, very good
a nit is the egg of a louse

explanation.surface: A cheerful report that a decent sort turns out to be useless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Good egg' reads as one phrase for a decent person, but it splits into two pieces that are then turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: Tinpot is an informal adjective for something cheap, inferior and of little value.

clue.text: Discussed Mrs Lovett's speciality line beside Tower

indicators.note: something discussed is talked over, so the pieces are to be judged by sound

parts.note: Mrs Lovett baked pies in Sweeney Todd
L is the abbreviation for line
on can mean next to, as in a house on the river

explanation.surface: Talk about Mrs Lovett's pies and a queue beside the Tower of London.
explanation.walkthrough: Mrs Lovett is Sweeney Todd's accomplice, who baked his victims into pies. Only the first syllable is a sound-alike; the line and 'beside' supply the rest as written.
explanation.definitionFit: A pylon is a tall steel lattice structure carrying power cables, a kind of tower.

clue.text: Recipe I supply; do I supply les ingrédients?

indicators.note: read as supple-ly, in a flexible way, so the preceding letters bend into a new order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cook lists a recipe and asks, in French, whether to provide the ingredients too.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'supply' is an adverb (supplely), not a verb. The French in the second half signals a French answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An épicier is a French grocer, the shopkeeper who sells the ingredients a recipe calls for.

clue.text: Like some rum special on the rocks?

parts.note: SP is an abbreviation for special
a drink served on the rocks is poured over ice

explanation.surface: A bar order: a special rum served over ice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the rocks' wants to mean ruined or anagrammed, but it is the bar term for served with ice.
explanation.definitionFit: Spiced rum is a familiar style flavoured with cinnamon, vanilla and similar additions.

clue.text: Competitive board meeting standard of e.g. Brie at reception?

parts.note: par is the standard or normal level

indicators.note: reception is what is received by the ear, as with a radio signal, so judge the piece by its sound

parts.note: of the nature of Brie, a soft cheese, is cheesy

explanation.surface: A boardroom meeting judged by the quality of the Brie served at the drinks reception.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Board meeting' looks like company business, but the board is a games board and meeting just joins the parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Parcheesi is an American board game derived from the Indian pachisi, played competitively with dice and counters.

clue.text: Units excitedly deal in preserves

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other

parts.note: to can food is to preserve it

indicators.note: acting excitedly means moving about wildly, so these letters are thrown out of order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Some units get stirred into a deal on preserved food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Preserves' looks like a noun (jam) but works as a verb in the third person.
explanation.definitionFit: The candela is the SI unit of luminous intensity, so several of them are units of measurement.

clue.text: Comparatively formal medic closes series on cooking

parts.note: DR is the abbreviation for doctor

indicators.note: cooking transforms raw ingredients, so the letters come out changed in order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A doctor closes out a run of cookery programmes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Series on cooking' reads as a TV cookery show; the doctor sits next to the cooked letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressy means smart and formal in style, and its comparative form describes something more elegant than another.

clue.text: Deviously work situation left chicken off when eating out

indicators.note: out can mean wrong or disordered, so the letters are put in a new arrangement
off means removed, so some letters are taken away

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for left
a hen is a chicken; these are the letters removed
taken as written, before the bird is taken out
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone engineers a way to leave the chicken off when dining out.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the hen from 'when' leaves W; that W, L and EATING are rearranged. 'Situation' belongs to the definition, not the wordplay. The hidden worm is ANGLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To wangle something is to arrange it by cunning or trickery, so the phrase means engineer the outcome slyly.

clue.text: Trimming beef, bar worker has cut double

indicators.note: bar means except or excluding, so those letters are taken out

parts.note: taken as written
the worker bee is the classic crossword worker; these letters go

indicators.note: something cut is shortened, so its last letter is lost

parts.note: a ringer, as in dead ringer, is someone's double

explanation.surface: A butcher trimming beef while a barman cuts a double measure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar worker' looks like a barman, but bar means except and the worker is a bee: BEEF minus BEE leaves F. The hidden worm is RING.
explanation.definitionFit: A fringe is a decorative border of threads, a trimming sewn onto clothes or furnishings.

clue.text: Mimic of gastronomy? Naturally

indicators.note: of means part of, so the letters are taken from inside the following words

parts.note: the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: Asks whether a copycat of fine cooking comes naturally.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark breaks the words visually, but the run of letters crosses it.
explanation.definitionFit: The myna is a starling famous for imitating human speech, so it is a natural mimic.

clue.text: It's rather creepy, chap out of university getting in our fourth drink

indicators.note: getting in means being admitted inside, so one piece goes within another
out of means without, so a letter is dropped

parts.note: a guy is a man
U is the abbreviation for university; this letter goes
a round of drinks plus IV, the Roman numeral four

explanation.surface: A man leaving college for the pub, where the fourth drink makes things rather creepy.
explanation.walkthrough: A round is a set of drinks bought for a group, so the fourth is ROUND IV. The hidden worm is ROUND.
explanation.definitionFit: Ground ivy is a low creeping plant of the mint family, so 'rather creepy' describes its growing habit.

clue.text: Last of bread and cheese is restorative, it's said

indicators.note: what is said is spoken, so the word is matched by sound alone

parts.note: something restorative makes you well

explanation.surface: A claim that the leftover crusts and rind are good for you.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last' reads as a single item but covers the end pieces of both loaf and cheese. The hidden worm is EEL.
explanation.definitionFit: The heel of a loaf or a cheese is its end crust or rind, the bit left over at the finish.

clue.text: Fray Bentos finally withdrawing their swan in a pie

indicators.note: pie is printers' jargon for jumbled type, so letters in a pie are muddled
withdrawing means pulling out, so a letter is taken away
finally points to the very end of a word, its last letter

parts.note: this letter is removed
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Fray Bentos, a British brand of tinned pies, dropping a swan pie from its range.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fray Bentos' looks like one name, but Fray is the definition. Remove the last letter of Bentos from THEIR SWAN, then muddle. The hidden worm is EARTH, across the gap.
explanation.definitionFit: Fabric that frays wears thin at the edges, and the phrase also means patience running out.

clue.text: Buffet by rail ultimately better value — and, like Across answers, one has the pick

definitions.text: like Across answers, one has the pick

indicators.note: to buffet is to batter and toss about, so letters are knocked out of order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the last letter of each word counts

parts.note: the final letter of each of the three words

explanation.surface: A railway buffet car offering a cheaper deal to those who book early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buffet' wants to be the train's catering, but it is a verb. The early bird catches the worm, and every Across answer has a worm hidden in it, the puzzle's theme.
explanation.definitionFit: An early bird arrives first and so gets first choice, just as the proverbial one gets the worm.

clue.text: Mean gunners tucked into an artichoke perhaps off table

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: something tucked into is pushed inside, so one piece sits within another
off means removed, so the named letters are taken away

parts.note: the artichoke is one example of a vegetable
taken as written; these letters come off
RA is the Royal Artillery, the gunners

explanation.surface: Artillerymen grudgingly eating an artichoke after it has gone cold off the table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Off table' sounds like a dish being cleared, but it is a literal instruction to strike those five letters from the word, leaving an incomplete stem for the gunners to sit inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Mean and average are both statistical terms for the central value of a set of numbers.

clue.text: Goes hunting game, wanting one?

indicators.note: game in the sense of lame or crippled, so the letters are knocked out of shape
wanting means lacking, so some letters are taken away

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written; these letters are removed

explanation.surface: Someone off to hunt game finds they want some piece of kit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Game' wants to be the quarry, but it is the anagram signal. Remove O, N and E from GOES HUNTING; the leftovers rearrange. Read whole, the clue describes the thing a hunter would want.
explanation.definitionFit: A gunsight is the aiming device on a rifle, which anyone going out shooting game would need.

clue.text: Declining light object into which one tipped juice

indicators.note: into which means something goes inside the preceding piece

parts.note: to demur is to object
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: something tipped up is tilted over, so the letters run backwards

parts.note: OJ is orange juice

explanation.surface: Describes a demijohn, the big bottle into which juice is poured for home brewing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Object into which one tipped juice' paints a demijohn, which is a false trail; object is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: Demi-jour is a borrowed French term for half-light or twilight, the dim light of a fading day.

clue.text: Ruined hut circles on verge of find in allotment?

indicators.note: to circle something is to surround it, so one piece goes round another
something ruined is wrecked, so its letters are left in disorder

parts.note: taken as written
on the verge of something is close to it

explanation.surface: A tumbledown shed on an allotment, a rented vegetable plot, where something is about to be found.
explanation.walkthrough: An allotment is a small rented plot of land in Britain for growing vegetables. The hidden worm is EARTH.
explanation.definitionFit: To unearth is to dig up out of the soil, exactly how you would find something in a vegetable plot.

clue.text: Tea for two cents no longer available, which is funny

indicators.note: something no longer available has gone, so those letters are taken away

parts.note: cha is tea, so tea for two is two of them
C is the abbreviation for cent, so two cents are CC; these go

explanation.surface: Tea for two no longer costs a couple of cents, which is a joke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tea for Two' is also a song, and the cha-cha a dance, but here cha is simply tea, doubled.
explanation.definitionFit: Funny ha-ha is the idiom for comic, as opposed to funny peculiar, so the word means laughable.

clue.text: See 14
Campbell's vegetable corporation goes short

indicators.note: something short is lacking its full length, so the last letter is cut

parts.note: a corporation is jocular slang for a pot belly, and tum is the stomach
a shy is a throw or attempt, so goes are shies

explanation.surface: A soup company's vegetable division is going under.
explanation.walkthrough: Campbell’s is the soup maker, but here Campbell is any Scot. Corporation as slang for a fat belly is old-fashioned British usage.
explanation.definitionFit: Tumshie is a Scots dialect word for a turnip or swede, the vegetable a Campbell would name.

clue.text: Why does it matter pork supplier's taken over Derby?

parts.note: a sow is a female pig
a derby is the American name for a bowler hat

explanation.surface: A business-page puzzle over why it matters that a pork company bought a Derby firm.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'taken over' places the first piece on top of the second. Derby is also an English city, which the surface uses.
explanation.definitionFit: So what is a dismissive retort asking why something should be considered important at all.

clue.text: Chap enjoyed dish, rather lacking out of the oven?

indicators.note: lacking means without, so those letters are dropped

parts.note: he is a male pronoun
as in enjoyed a meal
taken as written
-ish is a suffix meaning rather or somewhat; these letters go

explanation.surface: A man eats his meal, though it was lukewarm from the oven.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rather lacking' sounds like a criticism of the dish, but it removes -ISH, a suffix meaning rather, from DISH.
explanation.definitionFit: Food just out of the oven is hot, having been warmed through by cooking, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Like lobster, maybe, served initially covered in greenery

indicators.note: initially means at the start, so just the first letter is used

parts.note: the first letter
piny means covered with pine trees

explanation.surface: Lobster plated with a garnish of greens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Covered in' looks like a container signal but here it is part of the adjective for a pine-clad place. The hidden worm is PIN.
explanation.definitionFit: The spiny lobster, or crawfish, has a shell covered in sharp points, so lobsters can be prickly.

clue.text: Film juicy fruit overspreading area in garden?

indicators.note: spreading over something covers it on all sides, so one piece goes round another

parts.note: to hoe is to work a garden with a hoe

indicators.note: in puts the combined piece inside the next one

parts.note: a melon is a juicy fruit
A is the abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: A juicy fruit plant spreading across a patch of the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Garden' reads as a noun but is a verb. Home Alone is the 1990 comedy film. The hidden worm is MEAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Home Alone is the 1990 family comedy film about a boy left behind at Christmas.

clue.text: A record for starters at Nando's, not at Leon

indicators.note: starters are what come first, so only the opening letter of each word counts

parts.note: the first letter of each of the five words

explanation.surface: Ordering a starter at one restaurant chain rather than another.
explanation.walkthrough: Nando's and Leon are British restaurant chains. 'For starters' looks like a menu course but means first letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An annal is the record of a single year's events, usually in plural annals as a chronicle.

clue.text: Back to front division of e.g. brain protein

indicators.note: back to front here means the back letter goes to the front

parts.note: the brain is divided into lobes

explanation.surface: A biology note on how the brain is split into regions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back to front' usually means reversed; here only the last letter moves to the front. The hidden worm is LOB.
explanation.definitionFit: Globin is the protein part of haemoglobin and myoglobin, the oxygen-carrying molecules in blood and muscle.

clue.text: That has new stuffing for bird

indicators.note: stuffing goes inside, so one piece is packed within another

parts.note: the setter's host word, read as meaning that has
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: Something that has a new stuffing, ready for roasting a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about stuffing poultry; 'stuffing' only puts one letter inside. The hidden worm is INCH.
explanation.definitionFit: The whinchat is a small brown songbird of heaths and grassland, a relative of the stonechat.

clue.text: First to table ahead of bunfight, a theme on ship

indicators.note: first means the opening letter alone is taken

parts.note: the first letter
ere is a literary word for before
a bunfight is a jocular British word for a party, as is a do

explanation.surface: Setting the table before a tea party, with a nautical theme.
explanation.walkthrough: The theme is worms, so 'a theme on ship' is a shipworm. Here the whole answer is the worm rather than a hidden one.
explanation.definitionFit: The teredo is the shipworm, a boring mollusc that tunnels into the timbers of wooden ships.

clue.text: Empty A1 case of advocaat (light bottles)

parts.note: def is slang for excellent, as A1 is

indicators.note: to bottle is to hold inside, so one piece contains another

parts.note: an LED is a light-emitting diode, a kind of light

indicators.note: a case is the outside, so only the outer letters are kept

parts.note: first and last letters

explanation.surface: A first-rate case of advocaat, the Dutch egg liqueur, emptied with the light shut away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Empty A1' sounds like a finished case, but Empty alone is the definition. Advocaat is a Dutch liqueur made with eggs. The hidden worm is FLAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Something deflated has had the air let out of it, so it is empty and flat.
